Fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for a bank presentation (both null), so ROE/ROTCE are the return evidence. A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years.

base_override.reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (bank / auto lender): the engine's OCF-based conservative OE is rejected as the base — for a lender, OCF adds back the credit provision ($1,477M in FY2025, $2,166M in FY2024) and $1,397M of depreciation/amortization (dominated by operating-lease fleet depreciation) while the corresponding earning-asset deployment (purchases of operating lease assets $4,275M in FY2025; purchases of finance receivables and loans held-for-investment $5,249M) sits in investing, so OCF measures balance-sheet plumbing, not distributable earnings: FY2025 OCF $3,729M against net income of $852M, and NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE fires for 2023, 2024 and 2025. The result is a $14.5989/share normalized base (a 38.7% OE yield at $37.68) for a company whose diluted EPS was $2.37 in FY2025. For a bank, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy (the FUTU/LPLA/WSE/ARCC sector precedent in this sweep): SBC is already expensed inside it, the provision — a real through-cycle cost — is already charged inside it, and the median-of-3-FY normalization mirrors the engine's own base method applied to that definition. The median is also conservative for this name: all three years carry goodwill impairments on exited businesses ($149M / $118M / $305M) inside net income. Known upward bias, stated: total net income is used (the ARCC construction), so the ~$110M/yr of preferred dividends is not deducted — about $0.35/share against the common EPS series ($2.77 / $1.80 / $2.37, median $2.37); the verdict is sized with that bias in view. Declared under bounded authority (c): every input is a figure printed by this run's engine output.
base_override.source: Median of the last 3 fiscal years' net income per diluted share, built exclusively from this run's financials_history.csv (engine-filed figures): FY2023 net income $957,000,000 / 305,135,000 diluted shares = $3.1363; FY2024 $668,000,000 / 310,160,000 = $2.1537; FY2025 $852,000,000 / 313,043,000 = $2.7217; median of the three = $2.7217 (the FY2025 value)

description.text: Ally Financial Inc. (together with its consolidated subsidiaries unless the context otherwise requires, Ally, the Company, we, us, or our) is a financial-services company with $196.0 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025. The Company comprises the nation’s largest all-digital bank and an industry-leading automotive financing and insurance business, driven by a mission to “Do It Right” and be a relentless ally for all stakeholders. The Company serves customers with deposits and securities brokerage and investment advisory services as well as automotive financing and insurance offerings. The Company also includes a seasoned corporate finance business that offers capital for equity sponsors and middle-market companies. Ally is a Delaware corporation and is registered as a BHC under the BHC Act and an FHC under the GLB Act. Our primary business lines are Dealer Financial Services, which is composed of our Automotive Finance and Insurance operations, and Corporate Finance. Corporate and Other primarily consists of centralized corporate treasury activities (including deposit operations), the management of our consumer mortgage portfolio, the activity related to Ally Invest, Ally Lending, and Ally Credit Card, and reclassifications and eliminations between the reportable operating segments. We closed the sales of Ally Lending and Ally Credit Card on March 1, 2024, and April 1, 2025, respectively.

about.description_short: Ally Financial Inc. (NYSE: ALLY) includes the nation's largest all-digital bank and an industry leading auto finance business, driven by a mission to 'Do It Right' for its customers and communities. Ally is a U.S. financial holding company with $200 billion in assets and 9.6 million customers (June 30, 2026). Ally Bank, Member FDIC, offers online banking products, including high-yield savings and no hidden fee checking, and was the first major U.S. bank to eliminate overdraft fees. Ally also provides investing solutions through Ally Invest, including online brokerage, automated investing, IRAs and personal financial advice. As a leader in auto finance, Ally provides consumer and dealer financing, insurance, and vehicle remarketing services. Ally's seasoned corporate finance business provides capital to equity sponsors and middle-market companies. Visit ally.com.

analysis_md:
# ALLY — Ally Financial Inc.
v5 run, 2026-10-18. In scope (market cap $11.795B at $37.68, nasdaq_quote_api). **Finance sector — the OE/capex DCF fits banks poorly; confidence is low by rule, and the tier is a screen result, not a bank valuation. For this name the engine's OCF base is not merely imprecise, it is the wrong quantity entirely — see BASE OVERRIDE.**

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or the FY2025 10-K — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Financial-services holding company (bank holding / financial holding company) built from the former GMAC: the nation's largest all-digital bank (Ally Bank, $184.6B of assets within the group's $196.0B at December 31, 2025 per the 10-K) and an industry-leading automotive financing and insurance business, plus a corporate-finance arm lending to equity sponsors and middle-market companies. Q2 2026 (company release): adjusted EPS $1.21 (+22% YoY), adjusted total net revenue $2,276M (+10% YoY), core ROTCE 11.8% (vs 11.0% a year earlier), NIM excluding core OID 3.63% (+18bp YoY), consumer auto originations $13.3B (+21% YoY) on 4.6M applications, retail auto net charge-offs 1.57% (−18bp YoY, −40bp QoQ), Corporate Finance portfolio $13.7B (+25% YoY, reported 32% ROE in the quarter), 3.6M deposit customers (+7% YoY). GAAP common equity per share $44.38 and adjusted tangible book value per share $42.12 at Q2 2026 — the $37.68 price sits below both. Q3 2026 results are scheduled for October 20, 2026. Strategic scope has shrunk: Ally Lending sold March 1, 2024, Ally Credit Card sold April 1, 2025, consumer mortgage originations ceased in Q2 2025.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv, override-filled):** operating cash flow $3,729,000,000; capex $243,000,000 — by override, see OVERRIDE (capex); SBC $153,000,000 — by override, see OVERRIDE (sbc).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025 (engine definition): $3.333B = $10.65/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $3.333B, latest FY OE/share $10.65).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $2,006,000,000 for FY2025 in financials_history.csv — below the conservative figure because it starts from net income, but it still adds back the full $1,397,000,000 of D&A (lease-fleet depreciation included) while subtracting only the $243,000,000 PPE capex proxy, so it overstates a lender's distributable earnings too, just less. For a lender both engine definitions are approximations built on the same plumbing rejected below.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years on the engine's definitions. Net debt as the engine computes it is $11,735,000,000 (long-term debt + short-term borrowings − cash; a bank's $151,649M deposit base — its real funding — is not in this figure at all; see HIGH_NET_DEBT).

**Why the OCF base is rejected (see also BASE OVERRIDE):** FY2025 net income was $852,000,000 against OCF of $3,729,000,000. The 10-K cash-flow reconciliation shows the gap is structural, not a one-off: OCF adds back the provision for credit losses ($1,477,000,000 in FY2025, $2,166,000,000 in FY2024, $1,968,000,000 in FY2023) and depreciation and amortization ($1,397,000,000 in FY2025 — dominated by operating-lease fleet depreciation, with net depreciation expense on operating lease assets of $937,000,000 charged inside net financing revenue), while the cash deployed to create those earning assets — purchases of operating lease assets ($4,275,000,000 in FY2025) and purchases of finance receivables and loans held-for-investment ($5,249,000,000) — sits in investing activities, outside both OCF and the engine's capex leg. An OCF-minus-PPE-capex "owner's earnings" for a lender therefore counts the yield and the addbacks and none of the asset deployment. The engine's normalized base on that definition is $13.32/share and its latest-FY figure $10.65/share — a 35% OE yield at $37.68 for a company whose diluted EPS was $2.37 in FY2025. That is a measurement artifact, not a bargain signal.

**TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct, through Q2 2026):**
- OCF: FY $3,729,000,000 − prior YTD $1,887,000,000 + current YTD $2,724,000,000 = **TTM $4,566,000,000**
- Capex: **TTM $243,000,000**, all three legs filled by the override (prorated YTD legs cancel in the TTM math)
- SBC: **TTM $153,000,000**, all three legs filled by the override (same proration)
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **312,120,000**
- **TTM OE total $4,170,000,000 → $13.3602/share** — the TTM version of the same rejected OCF definition, quoted here because STALE_FY requires the check, not because it is used.

**Base used = median of the last 3 fiscal years' net income per diluted share, $2.72/share, via base_override (bounded authority (c)):** FY2023 $957,000,000 / 305,135,000 = $3.1363; FY2024 $668,000,000 / 310,160,000 = $2.1537; FY2025 $852,000,000 / 313,043,000 = $2.7217; median $2.7217 (the FY2025 value). For a bank, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy (the FUTU/LPLA/WSE/ARCC sector precedent in this sweep): SBC is already expensed inside it, and the credit provision — a real through-cycle cost that OCF adds back — is already charged inside it. The median is conservative for this name: all three years carry goodwill impairments on the exited businesses inside net income ($149M FY2023, $118M FY2024, $305M FY2025, per the FY2025 10-K income statement). One known upward bias, stated plainly: the construction uses total net income (the ARCC construction), so the ~$110M/yr of preferred dividends is not deducted — the filed common EPS series is $2.77 / $1.80 / $2.37 (median $2.37); the verdict below is sized with that ~$0.35/share bias in view.

## OVERRIDE — sbc (bounded worker authority, filing kind)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:sbc` — SBC missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 of the last 3. AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense was last filed for FY2020 ($80M, financials_history.csv) and ShareBasedCompensation is not filed at all, so the expense survives only in the equity statement and the share-compensation note. No tier was emitted, correctly.
- **The decision:** judgment.json carries `sbc_override = {value: 153000000, kind: "filing", source: "Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-25), Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity, line 'Share-based compensation': $153M for FY2025, with $167M for FY2024 and $159M for FY2023 in the same statement; corroborated by Note 23 (PSU/RSU expense $130M / $136M / $127M)"}`. In band: $153M vs the last filed value of $80M (override_checks out_of_band: false, 1.9x). The override fills ONLY periods where the tag is absent (sbc_tag = "OVERRIDE" for FY2016 and FY2021–FY2025 in financials_history.csv); filed values are never replaced.
- **Known imperfection, stated:** the single $153M value fills every missing period — it understates FY2024 SBC by $14M and FY2023 by $6M against the same equity statement (raising those years' engine OE slightly, ~0.3% of OCF — immaterial). FY2025 is exact. SBC is already expensed inside net income, so the override does not double-charge the NI base actually used; it charges the engine's OCF-based history, which is where the gap blocked the tier.

## OVERRIDE — capex (bounded worker authority, estimate kind, ack'd out-of-band)
- **The gap:** the preliminary run also exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:capex` — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 (and every other year) under every candidate tag: EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 40729 contains no PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment fact in any period, and the FY2025 10-K's Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows present no purchases-of-property-and-equipment line in FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025 — premises/IT spend is folded into investing "Other, net" (-$600M in FY2025) and cannot be isolated from the filing (the EWBC situation in this sweep).
- **The decision:** judgment.json carries `capex_override = {value: 243000000, kind: "estimate", source: "Anchor: FY2025 property and equipment depreciation of $243M, printed in the FY2025 10-K's other operating expenses table (with $224M for FY2024 and $196M for FY2023 in the same table) — the top of the filer's own filed FY2023–FY2025 range"}` with an ack_reason recording that the value is out-of-band by construction (no filed capex value exists under any candidate tag in any period, so no in-band estimate exists; the anchor is the filer's own filed depreciation figure). Maintenance PPE capex for a digital bank (IT hardware/software, premises, leasehold improvements) is proxied by its own PPE depreciation — the standard maintenance-capex proxy — at the top of the filed range, the conservative end. Net property and equipment was $1,150M at FY2025 on $196,002M of total assets.
- **Materiality:** immaterial to the verdict either way — the scored base is the NI-based base_override (net income already carries the $243M depreciation charge), and $243M is ~$0.78/share against the rejected $13.32/share OCF base. Its binding effect is binary: without it (and the SBC override) there is no tier at all.

## BASE OVERRIDE — measured impact
- **Measured impact (key_numbers.md, measured by make_score.py on the base actually used, same final configuration with overrides toggled off):** base OE/share $14.63 (no override) → $2.72 (with override), −81.39%; weighted IRR 52.88% → 13.54% (−39.34pp). Unblocks tier: YES — without the judgment overrides the filing gaps block scoring entirely, and without the base_override the score is the OCF artifact below.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-moderate; niche leadership that has not earned its capital
Justification: the nation's largest all-digital bank and a leading auto lender — against a commodity lending product with no structural pricing power, full consumer-credit and rate-cycle exposure, and a return history that proves the niche leadership is not translating into franchise economics. Fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for a bank presentation (both null), so the return evidence is ROE/ROTCE: GAAP ROE (fundamentals.json, on total equity) fell to 7.0% in FY2023, 4.8% in FY2024 and 5.5% in FY2025 — below the cost of equity three straight years, after 13.3% in FY2022 and 17.9% in FY2021 — and core ROTCE of 11.8% in Q2 2026 is a recovery print at a benign point in the credit cycle (retail auto net charge-offs 1.57%), not a demonstrated through-cycle level. Goodwill impairments in all three median years ($149M / $118M / $305M) on the exited card and lending adjacencies are a capital-allocation charge against the moat, not a footnote.
- FOR:
  - Auto finance leadership at scale — consumer originations $13.3B in Q2 2026 (+21% YoY) on 4.6M applications (+17%); dealer franchise plus insurance (F&I) attached to the same dealer relationships
  - Largest all-digital US bank — $151,649M of deposits at FY2025 (10-K balance sheet) funding the loan book; 3.6M deposit customers, +7% YoY at Q2 2026
  - Corporate Finance is a genuine second engine — $13.7B portfolio at Q2 2026, +25% YoY, with a reported 32% ROE in the quarter
  - Profitability inflecting — core ROTCE 11.8% in Q2 2026 vs 11.0% a year earlier; NIM excluding core OID 3.63%, +18bp YoY; adjusted EPS $1.21, +22% YoY
  - Credit metrics improving at the print — retail auto net charge-offs 1.57% in Q2 2026, down 18bp YoY and 40bp sequentially
- AGAINST:
  - Returns below the cost of equity through the recent cycle — GAAP ROE 7.0% / 4.8% / 5.5% in FY2023 / FY2024 / FY2025 (fundamentals.json); the franchise has not earned its capital since FY2022
  - Commodity product, no structural pricing power — auto loans and deposits are fungible; competition from money-center banks, captive lenders and credit unions sets the price
  - Consumer credit-cycle and residual-value exposure — provision for credit losses $1,477M in FY2025 ($2,166M in FY2024); operating-lease fleet of $8,772M carries used-vehicle residual risk
  - Capital-allocation record — goodwill impairments of $149M (FY2023), $118M (FY2024) and $305M (FY2025) on the exited Ally Lending (sold Mar 2024) and Credit Card (sold Apr 1, 2025) businesses; consumer mortgage originations ceased in Q2 2025
  - Rate sensitivity — NIM depends on deposit repricing and asset yields outside management control; interest on deposits alone was $5,302M in FY2025
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-18)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's g_base of 7.79% is not usable as printed for this bank. Its revenue series is the contract-revenue tag, which for a bank excludes interest income — the CSV revenue line is $1,244,000,000 for FY2025 against bank-total revenue of $7,914,000,000 in the same 10-K — so the blend's revenue CAGRs (5y 10.56%, 3y 11.06%) describe only the fee/contract slice, the latest-YoY component (3.84%) is that same slice, and the OE/share CAGR 2y of −11.63% is measured on the rejected OCF definition. The scenario starts were therefore set against the NI base actually used, via offsets (−0.157892 / −0.077892 / +0.042108 / +0.102108 / +0.182108 vs g_base) to −8 / 0 / **+12** / +18 / +26%. The pairing is deliberate: the base is a depressed median (peak provisions, $572M of cumulative goodwill impairments, trough ROTCE), so the base-case start carries the normalization that is already visible in the run-rate — growth holds 2 years, then fades over the 7.2-year CAP. Sanity check against prints: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS grew +22% YoY and GAAP total net revenue +10% YoY, and fundamentals.json's TTM bank revenue grew +11.5% YoY — the base start of +12% sits at the revenue print and well below the earnings print, the bull start of +18% sits below the adjusted-EPS print, and only the super-bull start (+26%) exceeds it, with this written reason: the earnings prints are recovery rates off a trough (FY2024 diluted EPS fell to $1.80), not steady-state growth. The bears carry the credit cycle this franchise actually has: FY2024's provision spike cut diluted EPS by a third in one year, so a −8% super-bear start on a 0.75 OE multiplier is a lived experience, not a stress fantasy. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $37.68.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -8.0% | 0.75 | Credit cycle turns hard: provisions spike past the FY2024 peak, charge-offs and lease residuals bite together, ROTCE falls back below the cost of equity | $11.11 | 5.87% |
| Bear | 25% | 0.0% | 0.90 | Recession-lite: earnings flat for years — provision normalization is eaten by NIM pressure and credit costs | $18.24 | 8.47% |
| Base | 30% | +12.0% | 1.00 | ROTCE normalization continues from the depressed median base (11.8% in Q2 2026 and rising), then fades to through-cycle growth over the CAP | $32.00 | 13.24% |
| Bull | 25% | +18.0% | 1.10 | ROTCE reaches the mid-teens and holds; auto originations and Corporate Finance keep compounding at print rates | $43.97 | 16.84% |
| Super bull | 10% | +26.0% | 1.25 | Recovery pace sustained: ROTCE expansion plus double-digit balance-sheet growth, credit stays benign through the fade | $66.75 | 22.69% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $32.94 (−12.6% vs price), IV@12% $44.34, IV@10% $57.10, weighted IRR 13.54%, base-case IRR 13.24%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 7.22%, terminal value 20.0% of IV@15%, scenario spread 6.01x, net debt 13.77x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end. IRR band: bear 8.47% (tier D) → bull 16.84% (tier B).
- One model artifact inside even this run, named rather than hidden: the engine subtracts its $11,735,000,000 net-debt figure (borrowings minus cash, deposits excluded) from the DCF equity value, while the NI base is already after interest expense on those borrowings — a partial double-charge that biases every IV here downward. It is one more reason the tier is a screen result at low confidence, and one more reason not to size to the point estimate in either direction.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:sbc / DATA_GAP:capex** (preliminary run): resolved by the filing/estimate overrides — see OVERRIDE (sbc) and OVERRIDE (capex). data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run.
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by construction — the TTM check was run (ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted in the Owner's earnings section) and the base was pinned by base_override to the NI median, which the TTM evidence corroborates directionally (TTM net income in fundamentals.json is $1,454,000,000, well above the FY2025 $852,000,000 — the recovery is in the run-rate, and it is carried in the scenario starts rather than in a TTM OCF base that measures the wrong quantity).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): resolved from the FY2025 10-K's own cash-flow reconciliation — the gap is the recurring non-cash bank addbacks (provision for credit losses $1,968,000,000 / $2,166,000,000 / $1,477,000,000 and depreciation and amortization $1,227,000,000 / $1,199,000,000 / $1,397,000,000 for 2023 / 2024 / 2025), partly offset by loans-held-for-sale flows and deferred taxes. There is no one-off to excuse: the divergence is the sector-model defect itself, and it is the reason the base is net income, not OCF (see BASE OVERRIDE).
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): accepted in full. A bank's distributable earnings are bounded by regulatory capital, its provisions are a through-cycle cost OCF only pretends to carry, its real earning-asset deployment is an investing flow, and value in banking is normally judged on ROTCE vs cost of equity and tangible book (adjusted TBV $42.12/share at Q2 2026; the $37.68 price is 0.89x it), none of which this model computes natively. Confidence is low, the base was replaced with the sector's honest proxy, and the tier is soft.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: see the OVERRIDE sections — gap, decision, single-value and proxy imperfections, and measured impact are all recorded in fields (judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json overrides_applied/override_impact, overrides_registry.json), not just here.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (6.01x): real — a consumer lender's outcome range across a credit cycle IS this wide (super-bear IV@15% $11.11 vs super-bull $66.75). Confidence is low (also mandated by the sector flag), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end (TIER_BAND).
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (13.77x normalized OE): an artifact of applying an industrial leverage lens to a bank, in both directions at once. The engine's net debt is $11,735,000,000 of borrowings net of cash; it excludes the $151,649M deposit base that actually funds the bank and the $133,964M net loan book that backs the funding. The leverage that matters is regulatory capital and credit quality: deposits of $151,649M against total assets of $196,002M at FY2025, an allowance for loan losses of $3,490M, and retail auto net charge-offs of 1.57% and falling at Q2 2026. The bear scenarios carry the credit stress this flag asks for; the ratio itself is not a solvency signal for a deposit-funded lender.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 8.47% vs bull tier B at 16.84%): accepted — the verdict spans tiers because the credit cycle does. Any position sizing belongs at the bear end.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range, and here it is extreme: the same final scenario set on the engine's native OCF base (normalized $13.32/share) prints **Tier S, weighted IRR 48.82%, IV@15% $161.24** — a fake S, produced entirely by counting provisions and fleet depreciation as earnings while their asset deployment sits in investing. On the NI base with through-cycle growth starts (−10 / −2 / +6 / +12 / +20%, the first recalibration tried) the same company prints **Tier C, weighted IRR 11.61%, IV@15% $27.08** (band D at 7.95% → C at 14.23%) — the low end of C: that pairing charges a depressed median base with mid-single-digit growth while the normalization is already in the prints, so it double-counts conservatism. The final run (NI base, normalization starts) prints **Tier C, 13.54%, IV@15% $32.94**. Anyone quoting one number for ALLY without its method is hiding the ball; both honest pairings land in Tier C (11.61% to 13.54%), and the verdict sits inside that range, not at its top.
- The bank cross-check the model cannot do agrees with C: at $37.68 the market pays 0.89x adjusted tangible book ($42.12) for a franchise printing 11.8% core ROTCE and rising, with a $1.20/share dividend (fundamentals.json dps_ttm $1.20). That prices in roughly cost-of-equity returns with modest re-rating — an expected return in the low teens, not the high teens and not single digits.
- What would change the verdict: ROTCE stalling at ~12% (the bull case is then the ceiling and even C is generous), a consumer credit turn (the super-bear is a lived FY2024 experience, not a tail), or the price falling to the weighted IV@15% of $32.94, at which point the weighted case itself clears 15%.
- Q3 2026 results land October 20, 2026 — two days after this run. The print (NIM path, charge-offs, ROTCE) is the next evidence on which scenario family is right; nothing in this score anticipates it.

## Final verdict
